memory_update.text: LEU should remain in the speculative_shadow lane for this node: strong HALEU/enrichment chokepoint evidence, but AI data-center power linkage depends on advanced nuclear deployment, DOE funding, licensing, and offtake.

POWL is a high-relevance equipment candidate for data-center power distribution, especially medium-voltage switchgear and custom power systems; risk is that attention and valuation have risen with backlog commentary.

MYRG and IESC are underfollowed infrastructure-service mappings: both can benefit from electrical construction, grid, substation, and data-center project execution bottlenecks, but require segment/backlog verification.

For AI data-center electricity supply, the actionable chokepoint map should split into four subnodes: regulated fuel-cycle inputs, generation/baseload assets, grid/interconnection construction, and inside-the-fence electrical distribution/infrastructure.

Need a later Layer 2 evidence pass on transformers, substations, interconnection studies, permitting consultancies, and testing/inspection vendors; this pass did not fully cover transformer OEMs or private bottlenecks.

node: Grid interconnection, nuclear fuel cycle, baseload power, and data-center electricity supply
summary: This Layer 1B pass expands the node toward scarce, regulated, or capacity-constrained suppliers beneath AI data-center power demand. The strongest underfollowed lane is not hyperscalers or large utilities, but: HALEU/nuclear fuel-cycle capacity, medium-voltage electrical distribution equipment, transmission/substation construction, and data-center electrical/communications infrastructure contractors. These names remain research candidates, not recommendations; later layers must verify backlog quality, customer concentration, permitting/regulatory dependence, pricing power, and whether AI/data-center demand is already fully capitalized.
